the calgary communities seeing effects of citywide rezoning the most and least the calgary communities seeing effects of citywide rezoning the most and least by adam macvicar global news posted december 23 2025 838 pm 4 min read watch citywide rezoning will be back on the table for calgary city council in the new year and new data shows where the impact is being felt the most while some innercity wards are carrying the bulk of redevelopment other areas including some with the most ardent opposition to citywide rezoning arent seeing much if at all adam macvicar reports the policy is called citywide rezoning but are the effects being seen citywide in calgary citywide rezoning approved by the previous council in the spring of 2024 changed calgarys landuse bylaw to make residential gradeoriented infill rcg the default residential zoning district across the city which allows for a variety of housing types including singledetached semidetached duplexes and rowhouses on a single property earlier this month the new city council voted in favour of kickstarting the process to repeal the policy and revert the citys landuse rules back to what it was prior to citywide rezoning taking effect what calgarians have told this council is that the blanket rezoning onesizefitsall approach hasnt worked to deliver the housing at a speed at a scale and at a price point calgarians can afford said calgary mayor jeromy farkas new data from the city of calgary shows there have been 478 development permits enabled by citywide rezoning since the policy took effect in august 2024 which created 1904 units prior to the approval of citywide rezoning those developments wouldve required a public hearing before the propertys zoning could be changed to make way for the development permit according to city data the bulk of redevelopment spurred by citywide rezoning are in ward 11 with 66 ward 6 with 63 ward 9 with 60 ward 4 with 58 ward 1 with 55 and ward 8 with 34 rowhomes and townhomes are the dominant development in each of the wards the area with the most redevelopment from citywide rezoning is ward 7 according to the city data with 127 developments including 75 rowhomes and townhomes a breakdown of the types of redevelopment enabled by citywide rezoning in ward 7 global news coun myke atkinson who represents ward 7 said the area has been disproportionately impacted by the amount of redevelopment even prior to the approval of citywide rezoning citywide rezoning allows for some of that redevelopment in other areas of the city he told global news my concern is that when we repeal citywide rezoning were actually going back to a time where the bulk of that development just falls back on the backs of the folks living in ward 7 however the development permit data shows there are some wards that have experienced very little redevelopment from citywide rezoning and others that have seen none at all a breakdown of the wards in calgary with little to no redevelopment from citywide rezoning global news the majority of the councillors representing those wards voted in favour of repealing citywide rezoning including ward 13 coun dan mclean one of the policys staunchest opponents ward 13 saw one townhouserowhouse redevelopment over the last year according to the data thats just the start mclean told reporters once you have a few on elbow drive or in canyon meadows then its cascading even more ward 12 coun mike jamieson whose communities havent had any citywide rezoning driven redevelopment said his opposition comes from how the policy was approved by the previous city council after an historic public hearing that saw the majority of the more than 730 speakers opposed to the idea close to 80 per cent were against it and council voted for it anyways he told global news for ward 12 they want a councillors thats going to listen and they want a city hall that works for them on important issues like this lori williams an associate professor of policy studies at mount royal university in calgary said the numbers show the issue and debate around it is riddled with nuance and politics people werent particularly supportive of ideology or partisanship in the last election what they want to see is representation of concerns within their ward she told global news thats not to say there cant be better policy formulated here but it ought to be on the basis of evidence and not on the basis of a speculative or ideological or partisan opposition however some councillors hope to overhaul the rules around what can be built under rcg zoning including ward 2 coun jennifer wyness who introduced a motion that asks administration to bring forward proposed changes to the zoning district to be considered during the public hearing next year what is the build form are we going to have scattered architectural designs thats some of the conflict thats come out of rcg theres no community context thats missing wyness said how do you redevelop so that those who live there are comfortable with it atkinson who voted against kickstarting the repeal of citywide rezoning said many of the concerns from the community around citywide rezoning enabled redevelopment wont be solved by repealing the policy as developers could still apply to build them even if citywide rezoning is scrapped there are many benefits that can come out of this when its done properly he told global news so the trick is to get the rules done correctly but when you havent had that development come in your neighbourhood its all about what you imagine it to be and your imagination always goes to the nightmares rather than the reality of the situation

i believe maga sits on the edge of a precipice their various factions are no longer compatible they entered 2024 with a strikingly unified posture elect donald j trump punish enemies and restore a certain vision of national primacy that objective worked trump returned to the presidency and the coalition that made it happen online populists evangelical institutions proisrael hawks and a newly emboldened cadre of tech elites celebrated itself as a political realignment but coalitions formed to win are rarely coalitions built to govern by late 2025 the contradictions within these groups were no longer academic consider the factions at issue first wealthy tech futurists and accelerationists they are drawn to trumpism less for nostalgic traditionalism than for power deregulation and statebacked dominance in strategic industries ai crypto defense tech and industrial policy reframed as national competition the 2024 cycle showcased a meaningful shift prominent silicon valley actors publicly embraced trump and reporters documented both the fundraising and the downstream cultural consequences inside the tech ecosystem their implicit bargain is transactional as they will tolerate populist spectacle so long as the administrative state is repurposed toward their preferred ends second christian fundamentalists and christian nationalists their aims are not primarily technocratic they want the moral state where family policy schooling sexuality censorship and jurisprudence conform to a particular theological anthropology that project demands discipline and purity not merely winning when they say politics is downstream from culture they mean it literally state power must be used to shape the moral ecology of everyday life third proisrael conservatives and christian zionists for decades this faction treated support for israel as a civilizational litmus test inside the american right that posture remains powerful but it is increasingly contested by younger more online segments of the maga base and by figures whose foreignpolicy instincts are closer to ethnonationalist nonintervention than to postcold war alliance maintenance recent reporting places senior maga figures especially vice president jd vance and speaker mike johnson squarely on this fault line fourth the groypers and adjacent whitenationalist networks however one labels them they are animated by identitarian hierarchy and a politics of grievance that frequently shades into antisemitic and authoritarian rhetoric mainstream outlets have described nick fuentes an emblematic figure for this milieu as a white nationalist and antisemite and the rights recurrent argument over whether to denounce or platform him has become a proxy war over the movements moral boundaries these factions can coordinate for an election because elections permit strategic ambiguity governing does not the most revealing cleavage is israel because it fuses foreign policy identity politics and moral boundarysetting in a single debate at turning point usas 2025 americafest one of the maga movements key convenings infighting over israel and antisemitism was not a side story it was the story major conservative personalities openly fought over who is welcome in the coalition whether antisemitism is being normalized and whether support for israel is a loyalty test or an encumbrance in a functioning political movement leaders resolve such disputes by articulating a hierarchy of values but magas comparative advantage has been the opposite a politics of maximal mobilization through minimal doctrinal specificity america first as a rorschach test here is the incompatibility in plain terms tech futurists want an entrepreneurial state permissive on markets permissive on innovation and strategically muscular abroad where it serves national advantage christian fundamentalists want a disciplinary state permissive for their ingroup coercive toward perceived moral deviance proisrael conservatives want a valuesbased alliance posture that treats israel as nonnegotiable groypers often want an identitarian state that is simultaneously antielite and comfortable with elite power so long as it enforces ethnic and cultural dominance while treating proisrael politics at best as subordinate and at worst as betrayal one cannot permanently fuse these into a stable program the nearterm consequence is an internal arms race each faction tries to capture the movements gatekeeping institutions media conferences donor networks and staffing pipelines so it can define real maga and delegitimize rivals the americafest clashes shapiro versus carlson disputes over fuentes and vances studied evasions the coalition is rehearsing a posttrump succession fight under the cover of current unity the longerterm consequence is more consequential for the country a fracturing coalition does not necessarily moderate it can radicalize when factions lose the ability to compromise they often seek legitimacy through escalation which can include purity tests conspiratorial scapegoating and symbolic conflict that substitutes for workable governance magas 2024 unity was real but it was instrumental instrumental unity dissolves when the instrument aka winning has been achieved and the bill comes due what remains is a movement perched on a precipice not because it lacks power but because it lacks a shared account of what power is for note this excludes the elephant in the room which is the epstein files how those fit into this equation is anyones guess
